# bugs #3303: Backslashes in source paths become control characters in the DWARF sections of an ELF file

- Ticket: https://sourceforge.net/p/sdcc/bugs/3303/
- Category: [Already fixed in trunk](../../fixed-upstream.md)
- Evidence: tested on r17176
- Recommended action: Close as fixed in r12964.
<!-- end of generated block -->

## Finding

The ticket reports source paths in `.debug_line` and `.debug_info` in which the sequences `\t`,
`\b`, `\f`, and `\n` of a Windows path are replaced by control characters. The reporter compiled
for stm8 with `--debug --out-fmt-elf`.

r17176 writes such paths correctly. The test was done on Linux, where a backslash is an ordinary
character of a file name. A source file whose name contains `\U`, `\n`, `\t`, `\b`, and `\f` was
compiled for stm8 with `--debug --out-fmt-elf` and linked. Its include directory has a name that
contains `\t`, `\n`, `\b`, and `\f`. Every backslash is doubled in the `.ascii` lines of the
assembly file. The listing has one byte 5C for each backslash and no control character, and the
paths in the ELF file are equal to the names on disk. No Windows host was used.

The defect never applied to mcs51. The port rejects `--out-fmt-elf` with warning 117 and writes its
debug information in the CDB format.

## Fixed by

[r12964](https://sourceforge.net/p/sdcc/code/12964/), which the last comment of the ticket names.
The revision adds `string_escape` to `src/SDCCutil.c` and calls it in `dwWriteString` in
`src/SDCCdwarf2.c`. `string_escape` puts a backslash before each backslash and each double quote,
and it writes a newline character as `\n`. `dwWriteString` is the only function in
`src/SDCCdwarf2.c` that writes `.ascii` lines.
